A normal resting heart rate for adults typically ranges from 60-100 beats per minute (bpm). However, it's essential to note that heart rates can vary depending on factors such as age, fitness level, medications, stress, and underlying health conditions.

Individuals who are considered fit and healthy may have a lower heart rate, while those who are highly active or have certain medical conditions may have a higher heart rate. It's also worth noting that athletes and very fit individuals can have heart rates as low as 40-60 bpm, which is typically considered normal for their age group.

In general, it's always best to consult with a healthcare professional if you're concerned about your heart rate or overall health. They can provide personalized guidance and help you determine whether a resting heart rate within the normal range is indicative of an individual's fitness level or overall well-being.
